newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African wool prices up at weekly sale.
newsitem.headline: South African wool prices up at weekly sale.

text.p: South African wool prices were up at the latest weekly auction, the Wool Board said on Thursday.
Of the total 8,120 bales on offer, 97.3 percent was sold.
Prices for 20 micron rose 3.0 percent, 21 rose 1.3 percent, 22 rose 1.6 pct, 23 rose 3.4 percent, 24 micron rose 5.5 percent and 25 micron rose 5.7 percent.
Bellies rose 3.3 percent, lambs rose 0.1 percent and locks rose 4.2 percent.
The offering included 1,759 bales of merino together with 1,475 other white, 298 bales Ciskei, 241 bales Lesotho and 508 bales of coarse and coloured.
Top-selling wool was 23 micron and 25 micron which sold 100 pct.
343 bales offered and 97.7 percent of 20 micron sold.
1,060 bales offered and 99.2 percent of 21 micron sold.
1,247 bales offered and 98.4 percent of 22 micron sold.
198 bales offered and 98 percent of 24 micron were sold.
The next sale will be held on January 15 with about 10,000 bales on offer.
